value.rationale: For a prescribed small community, the cross-cut size of a uniform tree is a natural network statistic; first-order Poisson heuristics give a+Poi(a). Its finite-host mean bias becomes observationally detectable at a sharp nonstandard n^(2/3) scale, with an explicit universal normal-CDF profile, while a corrected law remains accurate across every sparse-cut sequence. This is a meaningful strong-distance approximation boundary rather than a routine finite enumeration.
